featured_reviews.name: Swapnil Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Any BBC u visit is thd best in all senses, my always go to place and have a great time with family. I had serving of Mutton Biryani, a celebrated and aromatic rice dish that originated on the Indian subcontinent. The vibrant yellow and orange hues of the rice come from saffron or food coloring, while the garnish of crispy fried onions adds a distinct texture and flavor. Often considered a complete meal, a staple of Hyderabadi cuisine and is typically served alongside a side of raita or salad also we ordered some chicken Chilli as for the starters.

The staff here us very friendly, reservations available and the ambience is cozy loved it will visit soon.

featured_reviews.name: Rajesh Munj
featured_reviews.review_text: Had visited for dinner on Friday, so had a non-veg treat. Good ambience, courteous staff and service. All the dishes were very tasty. The rates are also normal. Convenient location near Korakendra flyover. Just loved the food and would definitely think of visitiñg again.

featured_reviews.name: Sania Serrao
featured_reviews.review_text:
Borivali Biryani Centre is a go-to spot for biryani lovers who crave rich flavors and hearty portions. This casual eatery has a straightforward, no-frills vibe — all attention is on delivering satisfying, flavorful meals.

The biryanis here are aromatic, perfectly spiced, and generously portioned, making them a hit with both regulars and first-time visitors. Beyond biryani, the menu also includes other popular North Indian dishes that complement the main attraction.

Service is friendly and efficient, and the place is ideal for a quick lunch, dinner, or takeaway. Borivali Biryani Centre is the kind of spot where you know you’ll get consistent, comforting flavors every time — perfect for a satisfying, casual meal.

featured_reviews.name: Anup More
featured_reviews.review_text: We went there in a group of four people and it was suggested by my friend as a popular eat out and the restaurant is the oldest or the main branch. We ordered Paya soup & Tulsi tomato soup for starters and both were amazing. The soups were right in taste, not too mild not too spicy. For appetizers we ordered hara bhara kebab & mutton seekh kebab, again, both were amazing. In the main course we went ahead with Veg & Chicken Dum Biryani, the biryanis were okay. As we were three people eating chicken biryani, we ordered full chicken biryani which was sufficient if you want to eat right else you go for a large size which would serve 4 people. Lastly we had custard pudding and blue mist as desserts and coolers. The pudding was very good. Overall, a very good place to visit for food, I can go again for Paya soup, mutton seekh kebab and custard pudding.

featured_reviews.review_text:
This space is a must visit if you:
𓌉◯𓇋 1. Want to enjoy sumptuous and delicious food, good ambience and happy vibes.
✨2. Enjoy a blend of classic and modern ambience
⚡ 3. Are looking for a quick yet delicious lunch/dinner in Borivali and neighbourhood.

featured_reviews.name: Saurabh Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is a restaurant 🏨 chain ⛓️ in Mumbai, known for its Mughlai 🍢 and non-veg food. I won't recommend this place much if you are Jain 👳or pure vegetarian 🥬. It's a 2 florey restaurant with AC 🌬️ and Non-AC 🪭 section usually the restaurant is packed during weekend. The name of the restaurant is BBC (Borivali Biryani 🍚 Center) known for its Biryani and majorly non-veg. If talking about the staff 🧑‍💼 they were occupied a lot and a bit ignorant about the customer 🙂, I asked 3-4 times for the same thing to different people still could not get much respond. The ambience ✨ of of Family restaurant and cleanliness 🧹 is maintained. Washroom is unisex and 🫧 clean however there was water blocked at some place.

Further, talking about the foods and the drinks that we tried :

1. Blue bliss - it's basically a lemonade 🍋 with an added food colour 🔵, it was sweet but an good option from the mocktail menu.

2. Virgin mojito 🍸- Just an old school taste of soda 🥤mixed with lemon 🧃 juice and with some basil 🌿 leafs in it.

3. Lemon Iced Tea ☕- It's a cool starter in drinks 🍷 to go with along with some heavy food.

3. Veg dum biryani 🌾- It's a simple option if you don't want to explore kuch and it's a safer option. I asked them to make it a bit spicy 🔥. A taste of mixed vegetables 🍆 and paneer served with boondi raita.

4. Paneer Crispy Plum  - It's a chinese sweet🍯 starter with some added veggies. I usually don't prefer sweets so I won't recommend the same.

5. Mushroom  🍄 Tikka - It's just like paneer tikka 🍢 but instead paneer mushroom 🍄 is used. For a change you can try mushrooms instead of Paneer.

The overall experience was okay as the staff was not attentive, the food taste in veg was not that good and I didn't have much to explore on the menu. You can go here for mughlai and kebabs dish 🍽️.

featured_reviews.name: Dipankar Meshram
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a good overall experience at Pancharatna Restaurant & Bar. The ambience inside is really nice and gives a pleasant vibe. It’s a good place to sit and relax with friends or family. The location is slightly inside a gully, so it may not be very visible from the main road, but it’s manageable once you find it.

Initially, we felt the cutlery looked a bit dirty, but later realized it’s actually part of their design/style.

Coming to the food – the taste was good overall. The chicken dishes were nice and spicy, just the way we liked them. However, the garlic naan was not that great; it was quite chewy and could have been better. The rest of the food was satisfying.

The pricing is moderate – not too expensive, not too cheap – reasonable for the quality and ambience.

Overall, it was a good experience, and I would consider visiting again.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited this place with my best friend on a Thursday evening this week.

It turned out to be their Thursday candle light dinner special with guitar and live singing, which we were not aware of.

Just 2 friends enjoying their beer in a dim ambience and an amazing Artist performing that evening (sorry, I don't know the name of the Artist). He was just awesome both locally and with guitar. He just set the whole vibe of that evening. Kudos to that!

If you order alcohol. You get unlimited Chakna (sides slong-with the alcohol), i.e., Salted peanuts, green salad, corn salad and papad with green chutney, all of this unlimited. They refill as soon as they see the bowls are empty.

Order took time to arrive, but continuous chakna refills made it easier to wait.

Staff is courteous and polite.

We ordered:
* Panchratna fried chicken 3/5 (they should serve this with a honey mustard dip or a tandoori Mayo dip, but they don't serve this with a dip by default). If you ask for a ketchup or a Schezwan sauce, you ll get it with no extra charges (points for that).

* Panchratna classic chicken Biryani, served  since decades 3/5

Location of the bar is a bit tricky as it is slightly inside the lane. Just get into the lane adjacent to Jaffer Bhai restaurant in Marine Lines, close to Bombay Hospital and you will see the bar right infront of you on the left hand side.

Overall. It was a very nice experience, must visit with friends or family.

Please note, my experience was totally based on a Thursday evening live singing vibe. Other days might have a different vibe.

featured_reviews.name: ishita Jain
featured_reviews.review_text:
Such a lovely place! The food was genuinely authentic South Indian and tasted amazing. Everything was super clean, which made the experience even better. The staff were incredibly warm, professional, and welcoming.
the decor is beautiful, the music sets the perfect vibe, and the hospitality makes you feel right at home. Great food, great people, and a great atmosphere. Definitely a place I’d love to visit again! ❤️✨🍽️

featured_reviews.name: sagar jadhav
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was my third visit to Santosham, and it continues to be a great spot for comforting, authentic South Indian food!
If you are looking for a complete traditional experience, their unlimited South Indian Thali is a must-try at least once. It’s a beautifully simple, home-style meal that tastes amazing. The thali comes fully loaded with a variety of authentic items—hot puris, steamed rice, flavorful and piping hot Sambar, a wonderfully tangy Rasam, and traditional sabjis like a dry Beans and Carrot Poriyal and a comforting Cabbage Kootu. They round it out with crisp appalams, fresh curd, pickle, and a sweet Payasam to finish it off. Just a quick heads-up: they have different pricing for the unlimited thali on weekdays versus weekends.
While the thali is fantastic and incredibly generous, it is quite a heavy meal. Personally, since we lean more toward classic South Indian snacks rather than massive authentic meals, the thali is a 'try it once for the experience' item for us.
If you aren't super hungry or just prefer lighter fare, absolutely go for their Idli and Dosa options instead. They are perfectly prepared and hit the spot every time. I also have to give a massive shoutout to their Dal Wada—it is incredibly crispy on the outside, perfectly spiced, and just flat-out delicious.

Staff is very helpful, one of the staff saw I m not adding Green chutney on rice, he came and suggested to use green chutney over the rice and it really tasted so good 😊
Overall verdict: Come hungry for the grand unlimited thali at least once, but you'll find yourself coming back regularly for the stellar dosas, idlis, and that amazing dal wada!

featured_reviews.name: Manikandan
featured_reviews.review_text: Santosham - Satvik South Indian Restaurant near Marine Drive is a clean and comforting spot for authentic South Indian vegetarian food in South Mumbai. The restaurant keeps a simple, traditional feel without trying to be overly fancy, and the food is the main highlight. Located in Marine Lines, it’s convenient after a walk along Marine Drive or nearby sightseeing. Service is quick, portions are satisfying, and the overall experience feels homely and consistent without being overpriced. One amazing thing is they serve meals and rice items throughout the day even at night.

featured_reviews.name: Shankar Kadam
featured_reviews.review_text:
Great place for authentic south indian food.
I had ordered THATTE IDLI, which was beyond amazing.
Loved it's feel, aroma and taste.
Sambar and chutney was too good.
Masala dosa too was very crispy,it's taste remains on tongue for significant time.
Overall enjoyed my pre- world cup cricket match , at Wankhede..

featured_reviews.name: Prachiti Parate
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had the perfect South Indian meal at Santosham after enjoying the beautiful view of Marine Drive.
We ordered the ghee masala dosa and ghee garlic masala dosa — both were absolutely delicious, crispy, flavorful, and perfectly made. The filter coffee was strong yet really smooth and comforting, just the way it should be

Simple food, great taste, and such a satisfying experience overall. Would definitely love to visit again!

featured_reviews.name: Gaurangi Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text: It was truly one of the best South Indian dining experiences I’ve had. The podi idli and the mini idlis with curry leaf powder were absolutely exceptional, rich in flavour, beautifully aromatic, and completely addictive. The dosa was perfectly crisp, the food overall was immaculate, the service was warm and attentive, and the ambience was stunning and thoughtfully designed. If you’re a South Indian food lover, you should definitely visit this place. Highly, highly recommended. ✨

featured_reviews.name: RACHNA TULI MASHKARIA
featured_reviews.review_text:
The banana leaf thali is not just a meal – it’s an experience that blends flavor, tradition, and hospitality in the most wholesome way. Served on a fresh banana leaf, the thali immediately brings a sense of authenticity and connection to Indian culinary roots.

What makes it truly special is the variety. From fragrant rice and comforting dals to vibrant curries, tangy pickles, crispy papad, and a sweet finish, every dish complements the other beautifully. The balance of flavors – spicy, tangy, salty, and sweet – ensures that every bite feels satisfying. The banana leaf itself adds a subtle earthy aroma while also being eco-friendly and hygienic.

Another highlight is the cultural warmth associated with it. The way servers lovingly add refills, encouraging you to eat to your heart’s content, makes the experience feel both generous and personal.

Overall, the banana leaf thali is not just good – it’s nourishing, soulful, and a celebration of food as tradition. Whether you’re a food enthusiast or someone who loves comfort meals, it’s definitely worth trying.

featured_reviews.name: Pranit Dhere
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely horrible experience at Delhi Darbar, Marine Lines branch. The chicken served to us was shockingly undercooked and unsafe to eat. When we raised the issue, the manager arrogantly refused to acknowledge the mistake. Instead of apologizing, he gave an absurd excuse saying it was “English chicken” and therefore cannot be fully cooked — which made no sense at all.
To make matters worse, he unprofessionally put his bare hands directly into my dish in front of everyone. It was humiliating, unhygienic, and deeply disturbing for all of us present.
Pathetic service, zero accountability, and unacceptable behavior. This place is a complete disappointment. Better to stay hungry than step into this restaurant.

featured_reviews.name: Dinesh r Vijlah
featured_reviews.review_text: Jaffer Bhai's Delhi Darbar he is know as Biryani king, to my utter dismay I have eaten better biryanis by home chefs, also the meat in the biryani looked suspicious but yes we had kheema and roomali roti which crossed my expectations as I had gone with the intention of having biryani, still I would say I would have to taste some more of his dishes to give him a total thumbs up. Till now Jaffer bhai the biryani king needs a put in a lot more to improve is Biryani.

featured_reviews.name: Atharva Mathkar
featured_reviews.review_text: I recently ordered the Biryani from Jaffer Bhai's Delhi Darbar, and it was easily one of the worst I have ever tasted. The experience was a major disappointment as the dish arrived in a very small quantity and was incredibly oily, making it difficult to eat. To make matters worse, the Biryani was filled with potatoes and the chicken pieces were subpar and not at all what we expected. Between the lack of authentic flavor and the poor quality of the meat, it was a total letdown that I wouldn't recommend to anyone looking for a decent meal in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: chintu das
featured_reviews.review_text: Worst biryani I have ever had. It was full of ghee and even had potatoes in it, which completely spoiled the taste. The prices are very high for the quality offered. To make matters worse, there wasn't even water available for handwashing. Overall, a very disappointing experience and a complete waste of money. I would not recommend this place.

featured_reviews.name: Amiit k Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had an amazing meal at Mao Family Restaurant–Best family Restaurant Kalbadevi-Best North Indian,Mughlai,Chinese,Arabian,Seafood Restaurant Kalbadevi! 😍

The Paneer Schezwan Khepsa Rice was packed with flavor, perfectly spicy, and loaded with delicious paneer pieces. The Manchurian Chatpata was crispy, tangy, and a perfect starter. The highlight was definitely the Hungama Khepsa Rice — huge portion size, rich taste, and enough to satisfy the whole group. Every bite was flavorful and satisfying.

Great food quality, generous portions, and excellent value for money. A must-visit place for Khepsa lovers in Mumbai! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

featured_reviews.name: Samruddhi Hambire
featured_reviews.review_text: Visited Mao Family Restaurant for lunch and tried the Hungama Kepsa (half) — good portion size and flavorful, definitely worth it. The Chicken Tandoori was outstanding; juicy, well-marinated, and something I would surely recommend to any non-vegetarian.However, the vegetarian menu was a huge disappointment. The Paneer Kepsa tasted more like a Chinese-style gravy than authentic Kepsa, and the Paneer Crispy was neither crispy nor made from real paneer — it was clearly synthetic. At ₹265, the quantity and quality of paneer were unacceptable.In short, this place is a delight for non-vegetarians but a nightmare for vegetarians.

featured_reviews.name: Sushant Kadam
featured_reviews.review_text: Service was quick. Their speciality kepsa even half is enough for 3-4 people. The waiter suggested us hungama kepsa as their most popular kepsa. It was worth the price. Had 3 types of starters inside kepsa. Only thing is table dining arrangement is not much spacious and you need to adjust accordingly.

featured_reviews.review_text:

. Taste is best. Quantity and quality both are good.. affordable compared to other restaurants. Supportive staff .. would definitely visit again..

featured_reviews.name: Strengers Fights
featured_reviews.review_text: The food quality at Mao Restaurant is very poor. The rice is often undercooked and completely tasteless. The overall quality of the food is extremely disappointing. Even the service is not proper, and the plates and bowls do not seem properly cleaned. I would strongly advise people to avoid eating here.

featured_reviews.name: bhavika jethwa
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Mao Restaurant and had an incredible dining experience! I ordered the Chicken Noorani Kabab and Chicken Tikka Mini Kepsa, and I must say, the kababs were absolutely delicious. They had a delightful tandoori coating, and the filling was made of perfectly spiced seekh chicken. The spice level was just right—medium spicy, which added to the overall flavor without overwhelming the palate.

What made it even more special was that it was served on a sizzling plate, enhancing the presentation and aroma. The Chicken Tikka Mini Kepsa was a unique addition to the menu, and being the first place to serve it definitely earned them some extra points. The taste was simply amazing, and each bite was a burst of flavor.

I would highly recommend Mao Restaurant to anyone looking for a great meal. The combination of delicious food, unique offerings, and excellent presentation makes it a must-visit spot. Can't wait to go back and try more dishes!

featured_reviews.name: Himanshu Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Subject: Complaint Regarding Food Quality (Delivery Order)

Respected Sir/Madam,

I recently ordered food from your restaurant through a delivery service. I ordered a half plate of Chilly Kepsa, but my experience was very disappointing.

The boiled egg in the dish had a very bad smell, which made the food inedible. This clearly indicates that the food was not fresh and raises serious concerns about hygiene and quality.

I request you to please look into this matter seriously and ensure that proper quality checks are done before sending food for delivery.

I hope you will take necessary action so that such issues do not happen again.

Thank you.

Yours sincerely,
Himanshu Gupta

featured_reviews.name: Abhilasha Akhade
featured_reviews.review_text:
I would never give the review or recommend this place to any one, On 17/04/2026, my friends and I visited the restaurant for dinner. After finishing our meal, we stepped outside and were waiting for a cab when one of my friends suddenly collapsed due to low blood pressure and fainted right outside your restaurant.

In that moment of urgency, I approached your staff requesting a small amount of sugar to help revive her. However, I was shocked by their response—they bluntly said they do not keep sugar. What was even more surprising was that at the same time, sugar was clearly available in the mukhwas kept there.

It was a matter of basic human kindness, and such a small help could have made a big difference in that situation. Unfortunately, the staff showed complete lack of empathy and humanity.

This is particularly disappointing because Kalbadevi has always been a place we frequently visit for lunch and dinner. Experiencing such insensitive behavior from your team was unexpected and unacceptable.

I do have a video of the incident, I will upload it soon. I will Raise a complaint too.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a wonderful dining experience at Balwas, Churchgate. The ambience is calm, pleasant, and perfect for enjoying a relaxed meal with family or friends.

I tried the Masala Prawns and a mutton dish, both of which were delicious and well-prepared. The restaurant offers a good variety of food options, catering to different tastes. The custard dessert was especially enjoyable, with a perfectly balanced sweetness that made for a great ending to the meal.

Overall, the food was tasty, the atmosphere was comfortable, and the service added to the positive experience. I would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking for good food and a peaceful dining experience in the Churchgate area.

featured_reviews.name: Faisal Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely disappointing experience from start to finish.

We waited for more than 45 minutes after placing our order, yet no food was served. Despite multiple follow-ups with the staff and management, there was little concern shown and no proper update on the delay. Customers should not have to repeatedly chase the staff just to get basic service.

To make matters worse, some of the plates and serving ware appeared chipped and damaged, which raises serious concerns about hygiene and attention to detail.

While the food itself was good when it finally arrived, the poor service, lack of communication, and overall management of the dining experience completely overshadowed it. A restaurant's responsibility goes beyond good food it also includes timely service, cleanliness, and customer care, all of which were lacking during this visit.

Unfortunately, not an experience I would recommend until significant improvements are made.

featured_reviews.name: the mk
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited BALWAS in Fort, and it felt like stepping back into the 1970s in the best possible way. The vintage décor, old-school charm, and warm ambiance give it a truly nostalgic vibe.

The staff is incredibly polite and welcoming, which made the whole experience even better. Now let’s talk about the food—absolutely top-notch! We tried 4-5 dishes and every single one was delicious, but the Chicken Lazeez stole the show. It's a must-try dish—rich, flavorful, and perfectly cooked.

Service was quick and efficient, and the staff made great recommendations.

Highly recommend this place if you're into good food, a cozy vintage atmosphere, and great service. Excited to hear they're opening a new branch in Marol soon—definitely keeping an eye out for that!

featured_reviews.name: MoinKhan
featured_reviews.review_text: I’ve been visiting this restaurant for several years, and it never disappoints. Every visit feels just as good as the first. The food is consistently delicious, with great taste in every dish. The portion sizes are generous, and the prices are quite reasonable. The ambience is warm and welcoming—perfect for family outings. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Aman Bhonsle
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’ve been coming here since I was a kid—long enough that I’m pretty sure my first real chicken tandoori happened right here. The menu has changed over the years, sure, but the place has stubbornly refused to lose its old-school charm. Portions? Still generous. This isn’t food that apologizes for itself.

The Chinese starters have absolutely nothing to do with China—and thank God for that. They’re loud, greasy, Indo-Chinese comfort bombs that slap hard. Pick any of the chicken gravies and you’re in a good place emotionally. I will say this: the kebabs feel a little smaller than they used to. Shrinkflation? Age? Betrayal? I don’t know. Still good. Just… noted.

Twenty-one years ago, when I was a broke college student and my parents would leave town—trusting me alone at home far more than they should have—I ordered from here like it was a civic duty. My friends from that era still remember how much food I could put away from this place. This is not health food. No one here is pretending otherwise. But it hits all the right buttons.

I ordered so often that before food apps, before algorithms, the guy answering the phone knew my order just by hearing my voice. Within an hour, like clockwork, the food would land at my parents’ place. I’d sit there demolishing it while binge-watching American TV, living my best irresponsible life.

Some of my old favorites are gone now, but the current menu holds its own. I’ve eaten here with my wife, with her family, across decades and phases of life. Parking is usually manageable. There’s a mosque nearby, Bombay Hospital around the corner, and the now-shuttered Liberty Cinema—where I watched half my childhood movies. The area isn’t glamorous. It doesn’t try to be. It’s old Mumbai, still breathing, still feeding people properly.

This place survives because it’s trusted. Because it’s consistent. Because people who know food still show up here quietly and eat without drama.

What’s instantly noticeable is who eats here.
Old-school locals, serious food people, and a steady stream of expats—especially Arab expats—who clearly didn’t wander in by accident.

Late at night, you’ll see many happy Muslim families settling in comfortably, sharing plates, unhurried, treating the place like an extension of home.

Go without hesitation.
Ask the manager what to order.

Then sit down and let them take care of you.

featured_reviews.name: tushar alphonso
featured_reviews.review_text:
​Stepping into DELHI RASOI is an exercise in managing expectations. If you're looking for sprawling dining halls, endless menu pages, or a spot for a large, rowdy gathering, this isn't it. But if you're a vegetarian seeking a perfectly executed, intensely flavorful meal that bypasses quantity for sheer quality, you absolutely must find this little 💎 GEM
​The space is small and intimate. The tables are close, the movement is restricted, and during peak hours, the atmosphere can feel more bustling. It has a focused, cozy, and slightly chaotic energy that somehow feels authentic—you know the kitchen is working hard just feet away.
​The starter and main course sections are intentionally limited. This might initially feel restrictive, but it quickly becomes RASOI's superpower. Instead of spreading its focus on Quantity, Rasoi concentrates on Quality, perfecting a handful of dishes.
The flavor is where this restaurant shines, brilliantly exceeding its humble surroundings. We tried the "Cheese Corn Ball, Paneer Chilli, Mushroom Chilli, Cheese Paratha" to start, and they were crispy on the outside, tender inside, and packed with a fresh, vibrant kick that felt utterly homemade. For the main, "Paneer Lababdar, Baigaan Bharta, Tadka Kadi Pakoda with Butter & Ghee Phulkas" was a revelation—rich, creamy, and complex, clearly cooked with ingredients and balanced spices. Every dish we sampled was bursting with deep, memorable flavor, proving that the kitchen staff are true masters of their craft.
​The verdict:
DELHI RASOI is the ideal spot for a quick, exceptionally tasty lunch or an intimate dinner where the focus is solely on the plate. Come for the fantastic food, not the fancy décor or extensive options. Just be prepared to wait a little, if you arrive at a busy time, and know that every bite is worth the WAIT.

featured_reviews.name: Amit Joshi
featured_reviews.review_text: This is a great place for simple, regular meals. Their phulka chapatis are soft and fresh, just like homemade, and the bhaji is full of flavor. If you’re craving a comforting, home-style meal, this place won’t disappoint. If you love mushrooms you must definitely try mushroom chilli 😍

featured_reviews.name: CA Mohit Shah
featured_reviews.review_text: We visited Delhi Rasoi Restaurant and had an awesome Punjabi meal. We tried Khichya Churi, Veg Chilli Milli, Veg Kolhapuri, Dal Fry, and Roti. The staff was excellent and accommodated our vegan request by preparing the food without dairy products. I highly recommend it to anyone who loves Punjabi food.

featured_reviews.name: Amol Pednekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
This place is now called as Delhi Rasoi (I don't know why they didn't update this on Google page).

Parking is difficult to get nearby.
Ambiance is good. Sitting arrangement is very comfortable.

We ordered Sarson Da Saag along with Makke ki roti & phulkas.
Sarson ka saag was good but heavy & loaded with oil.
Makke ki roti was good.
Phulas were very light & we really loved it.

Gajar ka halwa was tempting but didn't try it.
Overall a good experience.
